# Issuance

Token issuance refers to the process of increasing the supply of index tokens in circulation through minting.

This issuance process is defined below:

1. *User Initiation*: User initiates the issuance process by sending underlying assets via `issue(uint256 amount)` in the issuance smart contract, signaling their intention to exchange the assets for ***n*** AMKT tokens.
2. *Token Minting*: Upon verifying the correct amount of underlying assets received, the issuance smart contract mints ***n*** AMKT tokens.
3. *User Receives Tokens*: User is credited with ***n*** AMKT tokens in their designated address.

Markdown versions of documentation pages are available by appending `.md` to page URLs; this page is available as [Markdown](https://docs.amktdao.com/amkt-documentation/amkt-documentation/token/issuance-and-redemption/redemption.md).

# Redemption

Token redemption refers to the reduction of supply of index tokens through the action of redeeming index tokens for the underlying assets.

This redemption process is defined below:

1. *User Initiation*: User initiates the redemption process by burning ***n*** AMKT tokens via `redeem(uint256 amount)` in the issuance smart contract`,` signaling their intention to redeem the tokens for their in-kind value.
2. *Smart Contract Action*: Upon receiving the burn transaction for ***n*** AMKT tokens, the issuance smart contract verifies the burn and prepares to release the in-kind assets.
3. *Asset Release*: The issuance smart contract then releases the in-kind assets to the designated address provided by the user.
4. *User Receives Assets*: User receives the in-kind assets corresponding to the burned ***n*** AMKT tokens at their designated address.

All AMKT holders are entitled to redeem the underlying AMKT assets directly with the smart contract.

Full exact-match source and ABI bind its immutable Vault 0xf3bcedab2998933c6aad1cb31430d8bab329dd8c; pinned reads confirm Vault still designates this Issuance. issue pulls every current constituent from msg.sender into the immutable Vault using preexisting token allowances and mints AMKT only to msg.sender. Per constituent, required raw units are floor((virtualUnits+1)*amount/1e18)+1. redeem burns only msg.sender AMKT through Vault and returns each underlying token to msg.sender in floor(virtualUnits*amount/1e18) raw units. Neither method takes an arbitrary recipient or payload; no new approval, permit, signature or operator authority is admitted.

amount uses 18-decimal AMKT units; underlying amounts use each constituent native decimals. There are no per-asset input maxima, redemption minima, deadlines or amount>0 checks. The mutable nominal basket and allowances must be inspected before use; a precomputed quote is not bound against rebalance or nominal changes before inclusion. Both methods require a nonempty basket and post-operation Vault collateral invariant.

Pinned Vault state has emergency=false, issuance equal to reviewed target, two constituents (WBTC and wstETH), and inflationRate=0, consistent with current redemption and zero-fee documentation. Emergency can disable issuance but not normal redemption; observations are not continuing availability guarantees. The app marketing mentions 15 assets but current basket is not asserted to contain 15.

Current official mint/redeem portal and token/developer documentation describe normal basket issuance/redemption. Official docs foreground a redemption guide; Tally marks its DAO page archived and warns data may be stale. These facts are retained, not concealed or treated as standalone proof of a contract shutdown; no explicit primary sunset notice was located. The marketing root returned 404 and www certificate expired; use the functioning official app. No index reconstitution cadence, ongoing team activity or investment return is promised.

Vault governance can replace issuance/rebalancer, change nominals and fees, and set emergency responder. The AMKT token dependency is upgradeable, and constituent tokens retain their own operational/issuer risks. Full independent dependency runtime attestation, backing/safety assurance and governance actions are outside this inventory; no vault invoke/admin or token transfer functions are admitted.

review.callerFundingAndRights: issue loops current Vault virtualUnits and SafeERC20.transferFrom(msg.sender,Vault,...), then invokeMint(msg.sender,amount). redeem calculates fixed basket, invokeBurn(msg.sender,amount), and invokeERC20s to msg.sender. Caller cannot pick another source/recipient or executable payload; allowances are preexisting, no new signing or approval capabilities.
review.roundingAndUnits: SCALAR=1e18. Issue floor((units+1)*amount/SCALAR)+1 for each native-decimal asset; redeem floor(units*amount/SCALAR). AMKT amount is raw 18-decimal index token units. No positive-amount guard, deadline or per-asset slippage bounds.
review.lossAndFees: Vault nominal basket plus post-operation minimum balance invariant determines amounts; no minimum value/principal guarantee. InflationRate observed zero, matching official zero-fee proposal; governance can change rate. No fee collection capability selected.
review.pauseAndQueues: Vault invokeMint requires !emergency and current issuance authority; burn is issuance-only without emergency gate. Both require nonempty basket and post-action invariant. No asynchronous queue or ticket is created.
